copy.seo_title: Car Rental in Toronto | CarmaCars
copy.meta_description: Rent a car in Toronto by the day, week or month. Delivery to your door anywhere in the city, or pickup from us. Request with no payment up front.
copy.intro: CarmaCars is a Toronto car rental company with a small fleet of cars we know well. You choose a car on this page, send a request with your dates, and we confirm the car and the price before you pay anything. We hand every car over in person, at our location or at your address in any part of the city, from the waterfront to the 401 and from Etobicoke to Scarborough. Rent for a day, a week or up to {{maxDays}} days at a time.

sections.heading: How renting works in Toronto
sections.body: Pick a car below and enter your dates. Your request costs nothing and does not hold the car. We check the dates, then send an offer with the full price, the deposit and the kilometres included. If you approve it, you sign the rental agreement online and pay, and the car is booked. Before pickup we check your licence and identity. On the day, we meet you with the car, walk around it with you and note its condition, so nobody argues about a scratch later.

sections.heading: Getting around the city
sections.body: The 401 crosses the top of the city, the Gardiner Expressway and the Don Valley Parkway bring you downtown, and the 427, the 400 and the 404 run north toward the suburbs. Traffic is heaviest on weekday mornings and late afternoons, so plan airport runs and moves with time to spare. The 407 ETR north of the city has no toll booths: cameras read the plate, and the toll comes to us later. We pass it on at cost with a {{tollFee}} administration fee for each toll notice.

sections.heading: Delivery or pickup
sections.body: Collecting the car from our location costs nothing. Delivery to a home, an office, a hotel or a condo lobby anywhere in Toronto costs the delivery fee shown on each car's page. Tell us the address and a time in your request and we confirm both in your offer. For a condo or an office tower, add the visitor parking or the loading dock details, so the handover takes minutes rather than a search for parking.

faq.question: Can I rent a car in Toronto with a G2 licence?
faq.answer: Yes. We accept an Ontario {{licence}} licence for every car. Drivers {{minAge}} and older can rent, and drivers under {{fullAge}} pay a young driver fee for each day.

faq.question: Do you deliver anywhere in Toronto?
faq.answer: Yes. We deliver to any address in the city for the car's delivery fee, and we can collect the car from you at the end.

faq.question: Do I pay when I send a request?
faq.answer: No. The request is free and does not hold the car. You pay only after we confirm the car and the price and you approve the offer.

faq.question: How are 407 ETR tolls billed?
faq.answer: The toll is billed to the car's plate and comes to us. We charge you the toll at cost plus {{tollFee}} for each notice, on a statement after the rental.

copy.seo_title: Car Rental in Downtown Toronto | CarmaCars
copy.meta_description: Rent a car in downtown Toronto with delivery to your condo, hotel or office. No counter and no line: we hand the car over to you in person.
copy.intro: Downtown is where a car is hardest to pick up and easiest to do without, until the day you need one. We bring the car to you instead: to a condo lobby in CityPlace, a hotel on Front Street, an office in the Financial District or a loft in the Distillery District. You send a request with the address and the time, we confirm the car and the price, and a member of our team meets you with it. No rental counter, no shuttle and no line.

sections.heading: Handovers in the core
sections.body: Downtown streets are tight, so a good handover is planned. Tell us whether there is visitor parking, a loading dock, a hotel valet lane or a laneway where we can stop for a few minutes. We walk around the car with you, take photos of its condition, check your licence and the card you paid with, and show you the controls. Then the car is yours. At the end of the rental we can collect it from the same place, or you can return it to our location.

sections.heading: Parking and driving downtown
sections.body: Most condo buildings have a few visitor spaces that need a permit from the concierge, and Green P runs municipal garages and lots across the core. Street parking is metered and limited in time, and rush hour rules on main streets mean a parked car can be towed. Read the signs before you leave the car. To get out of the core, the Gardiner Expressway runs west along the lake and the Don Valley Parkway runs north. Lake Shore Boulevard is the slower road beside the Gardiner.

sections.heading: Weekend trips from downtown
sections.body: Many downtown renters live without a car and rent one for a weekend at a cottage, a trip to see family or a big shopping run. Book a car that leaves on Friday and comes back on Sunday or Monday, and we can deliver it to your building on Friday evening. Each car's page shows its weekend day rate and the kilometres included, added up over the whole trip.

faq.question: Can you deliver the car to my condo?
faq.answer: Yes. Give us the address and tell us about visitor parking or the loading area, and we meet you there at the time we agree.

faq.question: Where do I park a rental car downtown?
faq.answer: Visitor parking in your building, a Green P garage or lot, or a metered street space within its time limit. Fines and towing charges during the rental are the renter's.

faq.question: Can I return the car downtown?
faq.answer: Yes. We can collect it from your address at the end for the car's return pickup fee, or you can bring it back to our location at no charge.

faq.question: Do I need my own insurance policy?
faq.answer: Third-party liability coverage is included in the rate. For damage to the car you choose one of three options before pickup, explained on our requirements page.

copy.seo_title: Car Rental in North York | CarmaCars
copy.meta_description: Rent a car in North York with delivery to Willowdale, Don Mills, York University and more. Daily, weekly and monthly rates on every car.
copy.intro: North York sits on both sides of the 401, which makes it a good base for a rental: Yorkdale, the 400 and the airport to the west, the 404 and Markham to the east. We deliver to homes and condos around Yonge and Sheppard, Willowdale, Bayview Village and Don Mills, and to the York University area. Pick a car below, send a request with your dates and address, and we confirm everything before you pay.

sections.heading: Delivery in North York
sections.body: Many of our North York renters live in the condo towers along Yonge Street between Sheppard and Finch. Visitor parking there is short, so tell us the building's rules when you send your request. For houses in Willowdale or Don Mills we can meet you in the driveway. The car's delivery fee covers the trip to you, and we can collect it again at the end of the rental.

sections.heading: Highways and transit
sections.body: The 401 runs through the middle of North York and is one of the busiest highways in North America, so give yourself time at rush hour. The 404 and the Don Valley Parkway start where they meet the 401 near Don Mills, and Allen Road links the 401 with midtown. If you arrive by subway, Line 1 stops at Sheppard-Yonge and North York Centre, and Line 4 runs east along Sheppard to Don Mills. We can meet you near a station when that is easier.

sections.heading: Longer rentals
sections.body: Students near York University and people between leases often rent for a few weeks at a time. A rental of {{weekFrom}} days or more is priced at the weekly rate, and up to {{maxDays}} days at the monthly rate, whichever costs less. When a monthly rental ends you can renew it with a new agreement, and the deposit carries over.

faq.question: Do you deliver to York University?
faq.answer: Yes. We deliver to residences and nearby homes, and we can agree a meeting point on campus when parking is hard.

faq.question: Can I pick up the car near a subway station?
faq.answer: Yes. Tell us which station suits you and we agree a place nearby where the car can stop safely.

faq.question: Is there a minimum rental length?
faq.answer: One day. A day is 24 hours from your pickup time.

faq.question: How do I return the car?
faq.answer: We collect it from your address for the car's return pickup fee, or you bring it back to our location at no charge.

copy.seo_title: Car Rental in Scarborough | CarmaCars
copy.meta_description: Rent a car in Scarborough with delivery to your home or a meeting point near Scarborough Town Centre. Request with no payment up front.
copy.intro: Scarborough is big, spread out and built around the car, and the transit gaps show the moment you need to get to the zoo, the Bluffs or a relative across town. We deliver rental cars to homes in Agincourt, Malvern, Guildwood and Birch Cliff, and to meeting points near Scarborough Town Centre. Choose a car below and send a request; you pay only after we confirm the car and the price.

sections.heading: Where we meet you
sections.body: For a house we usually meet you in the driveway. For an apartment building, tell us about visitor parking. If neither works, the large parking areas around Scarborough Town Centre make an easy place to hand over a car. We check your licence and card, walk around the car with you and show you how everything works.

sections.heading: Driving from Scarborough
sections.body: The 401 crosses Scarborough from east to west and takes you downtown by the Don Valley Parkway or north to Markham and beyond. Kingston Road follows the lake toward the Bluffs and Guildwood. Line 2 of the subway ends at Kennedy station, so a car is often the quickest way to the eastern edge of the city, the Toronto Zoo and the Rouge.

sections.heading: Family trips and big shopping runs
sections.body: If you are moving furniture, collecting family from the airport or heading out for a day at the zoo, filter the cars below by seats and size. Each car's page lists its seats, its luggage space where we have measured it, and the kilometres included each day.

faq.question: Do you deliver in Scarborough?
faq.answer: Yes, to any address, for the car's delivery fee. We can also meet you at an agreed spot near Scarborough Town Centre.

faq.question: Can young drivers rent in Scarborough?
faq.answer: Drivers {{minAge}} and older with an Ontario {{licence}} licence can rent, and each car's page says whether it takes drivers aged {{youngA}}. Drivers under {{fullAge}} pay a young driver fee for each day.

faq.question: Can I drive the car outside Toronto?
faq.answer: Yes, anywhere in Ontario. Leaving the province needs our written agreement first, so ask in your request.

faq.question: What happens if the car breaks down?
faq.answer: Roadside assistance is included around the clock. Call the number on your agreement and we arrange help.

sections.body: The towers along Lake Shore Boulevard at Humber Bay Shores have busy driveways and short visitor parking. Tell us your building's rules and we time the handover so it takes a few minutes. For houses in Mimico, Long Branch and The Kingsway we meet you at the door. Subway riders can meet us near Kipling or Islington station.

sections.heading: Renting before a flight
sections.body: If you live in Etobicoke and fly from Pearson, you can rent a car that ends at the airport, or keep it for the trip there and back. Delivery to the airport is priced in your offer, and an airport surcharge may apply.

faq.question: Can you deliver to Humber Bay Shores?

faq.question: Is Etobicoke close to Pearson?

faq.question: How do I pay?
faq.answer: After we confirm the car and the price, you approve the offer, sign the agreement online and pay with a credit card in your name.

faq.question: Is there a deposit?
faq.answer: Yes. Each car's page shows its deposit. It is taken about {{depLead}} before pickup, never when you book.

Ending a rental at Pearson works the same way in reverse: we agree the time and place, and collect the car from you.

sections.heading: Travelling without a car first

faq.question: Do you have a counter at Pearson?

faq.question: What if my flight is delayed?

faq.question: Can I return the car at the airport?

faq.question: Which terminal do you serve?

articles.summary: Drivers {{minAge}} and older with an Ontario {{licence}} licence can rent from CarmaCars. Here is what it costs and what to bring.
articles.body_md:
Renting a car under 25 in Toronto has a reputation for being hard or expensive. Many companies set the minimum age at 21 or 25, and some only let younger drivers take a few small cars. CarmaCars rents to drivers {{minAge}} and older, on almost every car in the fleet. This guide explains the rules, the fees and the small things that make a first rental go smoothly.

## Who can rent

You can rent if you are {{minAge}} or older on the day of pickup and hold an Ontario {{licence}} licence that is valid for the whole rental. A G2 licence is fine: you do not need your full G. Your licence must be the original card, not a photo, and the name on it must match the name on the booking and the credit card.

Each car's page says whether it takes drivers aged {{youngA}}. Almost all of them do. If a car does not, the request form tells you before you send it.

## The young driver fee

Drivers under {{fullAge}} pay a young driver fee for each day of the rental. There are two age bands:

- Ages {{youngA}}: usually {{ydA}} a day
- Ages {{youngB}}: usually {{ydB}} a day

Some cars have their own fee, shown on the car's page. There is no maximum, so a long rental adds up. The fee is a separate line in your offer, and you see the total before you pay anything. If you add another driver under {{fullAge}}, the fee applies to them as well.

## What you need before pickup

You need a credit card in your own name. It pays for the rental and holds the deposit, which is taken about {{depLead}} before pickup, never when you book. Debit cards and prepaid cards are not accepted, and a parent's card cannot be used for your rental.

Before pickup we check your identity. You upload photos of the front and back of your licence and a selfie, and a member of our team compares them. It takes a few minutes of your time, and it means the handover itself is quick.

For damage to the car, you need one of three coverage options in place before pickup. Our requirements page explains each one. Third-party liability coverage is already included in the rate.

## On the day

We meet you with the car, at our location or at your address. We check your original licence and the card you paid with, then walk around the car together. Point out every mark you see, even a small one: we photograph each one, and those photos protect you at the return. Ask about anything you are unsure of, such as how to open the fuel door or connect your phone.

## Avoiding surprise charges

Most extra charges on a first rental come from a few things:

- **Fuel.** Return the car with the same fuel it had at pickup. If it is lower, we refuel it at the pump price plus {{fuelPct}}, plus a {{fuelFee}} service fee.
- **Tolls.** The 407 ETR has no booths. Cameras read the plate and the toll is billed to us weeks later. We charge it at cost plus {{tollFee}} for each notice. Most map apps have an option to avoid tolls.
- **Kilometres.** Each car includes a daily allowance, added up over the rental. Past it, each kilometre costs between {{overMin}} and {{overMax}}, depending on the car.
- **Late returns.** Tell us early if you are running late. The agreement explains how a late return is charged.
- **Parking and speeding tickets.** They are yours, plus {{ticketFee}} for each one we process.

## Adding a second driver

If a friend or partner will share the driving, add them to your request. Every driver meets the same rules: the age, an Ontario {{licence}} licence and the identity check. Each additional driver costs {{addDrvPct}} of the daily rate for each day, and a driver under {{fullAge}} also pays the young driver fee. Only drivers named on the agreement may drive the car, so add everyone before pickup.

## If something goes wrong

Roadside assistance is included around the clock. If the car breaks down, get to a safe place and call the number on your agreement. After a collision, make sure everyone is safe, call the police if anyone is hurt, take photos, and tell us as soon as you can. Young drivers are not treated differently here: the same rules and the same deductible of {{deductible}} apply to everyone.

## Getting the best price

Book a week rather than a few separate days: a trip of 1 to {{weekFromLess1}} days is capped at the weekly rate. If your plans are fixed, the non-refundable option takes {{nonRef}} off the rental charge. And if you can collect the car from our location, you save the delivery fee.

articles.title: 407 ETR tolls in a rental car: what you pay and how it is billed
articles.seo_title: 407 ETR Tolls in a Rental Car: How Billing Works
articles.description: How the 407 ETR bills a rental car without a transponder, why the toll arrives weeks later, what CarmaCars charges, and how to avoid tolls in the GTA.
articles.summary: The 407 ETR has no toll booths. Here is how its tolls reach a rental car, and what we charge you for them.
articles.body_md:
The 407 ETR is the toll highway that crosses the top of the Greater Toronto Area, from Burlington in the west to the Durham Region in the east. It is often the fastest way around the city at rush hour. It also has no toll booths at all, which surprises many people driving a rental for the first time. This guide explains how the tolls work and what you pay when you use it in a CarmaCars car.

## How the 407 ETR charges

There are no gates and no booths. Cameras on gantries above the road photograph the licence plate of every vehicle that enters and leaves. The highway's operator then bills the vehicle's registered owner by mail.

A trip on the 407 ETR is usually made up of:

- a toll for each kilometre, which depends on the section of highway, the time of day and the day of the week,
- a charge for each trip,
- a camera charge, because a rental car does not have a transponder.

The rates change, and the operator publishes them on its own website. For a short hop the total is modest; for a long trip at rush hour it can be a meaningful part of a day's rental.

## How the toll reaches you

Because the car is registered to us, the bill comes to us, often several weeks after your rental. We match each toll notice to the booking that had the car at that date and time, and charge it to you at cost, plus a {{tollFee}} administration fee for each notice. The charge appears on a statement after the rental, and the card on file pays it.

That is why a toll can show up long after you returned the car. It is not an error: the highway simply bills slowly.

## How to avoid tolls

You never have to use the 407 ETR. The 401 runs parallel to it, a little further south, and it is free. Most map apps have a setting to avoid toll roads; switch it on before you set off and the route will keep you off the 407 ETR.

Signs at every entrance ramp show that the 407 ETR is a toll road, usually in blue and with the highway's own logo. If you see one and do not want to pay, take the next free road instead.

## When the 407 ETR is worth it

If you are crossing the GTA at rush hour, for example from Pearson to Markham or from Oakville to Vaughan, the 407 ETR can save a lot of time. For an airport run with a flight to catch, many renters decide that the toll is worth paying. Just know that it will arrive later, with the {{tollFee}} fee added.

## Checking a toll charge

Each toll we charge shows the date and time of the trip and the amount on the notice, so you can match it to your own plans. If a toll does not look like yours, for example a trip on a day you had already returned the car, tell us. We check the booking and the times, and remove a charge that belongs to someone else.

## Other charges that arrive after a rental

Tolls are not the only thing that can reach us after you return the car. Parking tickets and camera speeding or red light tickets are also sent to the registered owner. We match them to your booking and charge them to you, plus {{ticketFee}} for each ticket we process. If you think a ticket is wrong, tell us: we can give you what you need to dispute it.

faq.answer: Use the 401 instead, and switch on the avoid tolls setting in your map app.

articles.body_md:
Renting a car should not involve surprises at the counter. With CarmaCars there is no counter, but there are still a few things you need before we hand you the keys. This checklist covers all of them, in the order they come up.

## Before you send a request

- **Age.** You must be {{minAge}} or older. Drivers under {{fullAge}} pay a young driver fee for each day.
- **Licence.** An Ontario {{licence}} licence, valid for the whole rental. Bring the original card on the day.
- **Credit card.** A credit card in your own name, for the payment and the deposit. Debit and prepaid cards are not accepted.

Sending a request is free. It does not hold the car and takes no payment. Choose a car, enter your dates, tell us whether you want delivery, and send it.

## The offer

We check the dates and send you an offer with the full price: the rental charge, any fees, HST at {{hst}}, the deposit and the kilometres included. An offer stays open for {{offerHours}} hours. If you approve it, you sign the rental agreement online and pay, and the car is booked for you. Until then, someone else can book the same car.

## The identity check

Before pickup you upload photos of the front and back of your licence and a selfie. A member of our team compares them and confirms your identity. Every additional driver does the same. Do this as soon as you have booked, so there is time to fix a blurry photo.

## Coverage for damage

Third-party liability coverage is included in every rental. For damage to the car itself you need one of three options in place before pickup:

1. Coverage under your own auto policy that extends to a rental car.
2. Rental car coverage from your credit card, where the card offers it.
3. The CarmaCars Protection Plan.

Our requirements page explains each option and what to show us. If the car is damaged, repairs under {{deductible}} are billed at cost, and from {{deductible}} we claim on our fleet policy and you pay the {{deductible}} deductible.

## The deposit

Each car has a deposit, shown on its page. It is taken about {{depLead}} before pickup, never when you book. For rentals of {{holdDays}} days or less it is a hold on your card; for longer rentals it is charged and refunded. We release the balance within {{releaseDays}} after you return the car.

## At pickup

We meet you with the car at our location or at your address. Bring your original licence and the card you paid with. We walk around the car together and photograph its condition, note the fuel and the kilometres, and show you the controls.

## Additional drivers

Anyone else who will drive must be on the booking. Every driver meets the same rules, does the identity check and signs the agreement. Each additional driver adds {{addDrvPct}} of the daily rate for each day.

## If your plans change

You can cancel from your account. Within {{cGrace}} hours of booking, when pickup is {{cEarly}} hours or more away, you get {{c1}} back. Otherwise {{cEarly}} hours or more before pickup returns {{c2}}, and {{cLate}} to {{cEarly}} hours before returns {{c3}}. Less than {{cLate}} hours before pickup, or a no-show, is not refunded. A non-refundable booking is not refunded at all, in exchange for its {{nonRef}} discount.

## At return

Bring the car back at the agreed time with the same fuel or charge it had at pickup, and take your things out. We check it with you and photograph it again. Tolls and tickets that arrive later are charged to the card on file with their administration fees.

articles.summary: No counter and no shuttle: we bring the car to you at Pearson, at a meeting point confirmed in advance.
articles.body_md:
Toronto Pearson is the busiest airport in Canada, and picking up a rental there usually means a walk, a line at a counter and a shuttle to a parking lot. CarmaCars does not have a counter at the airport. Instead, we bring the car to you at a meeting point we confirm before you land. This guide explains how it works.

## Before you fly

Send a request for the car you want, with your pickup date and time, and choose delivery to the airport. In the notes, add:

- your airline and flight number,
- your terminal, if you know it,
- a phone number that works when you land.

We send an offer with the full price. Airport delivery is priced in the offer, and an airport surcharge may apply. Once you approve the offer, sign and pay, the car is booked. Do the identity check before you travel, so nothing is left to do at the airport.

## When you land

Before pickup we confirm the meeting point and the number to call. When you have your bags, call or message us. A member of our team meets you with the car, checks your original licence and the card you paid with, and walks around the car with you while we photograph its condition. Then the keys are yours.

## If your flight is late

Flights are delayed all the time. Message us with the new arrival time as soon as you know it, and we adjust the handover. If the delay is long, we may agree a new time with you.

## Driving away from Pearson

The airport sits between the 427, the 401 and the 409. The 427 takes you south toward Etobicoke and downtown by the Gardiner Expressway, and the 401 runs east and west. The 407 ETR is close by to the north: it is a toll road with no booths, and its tolls are billed to us and passed on at cost with {{tollFee}} for each notice. If you would rather avoid tolls, switch on the avoid tolls setting in your map app before you leave.

## Returning the car before a flight

You can end your rental at Pearson too. Agree a time and a meeting point with us, and leave plenty of time before your flight. Return the car with the fuel or charge it had at pickup, and check the seats and the trunk for your things. We check the car with you, and you head to the terminal.

## Choosing a car for an airport run

Think about luggage before you choose. Each car's page lists its seats and, where we have measured it, how many large bags fit in the trunk. A family of four with four big suitcases usually needs an SUV or a minivan rather than a compact car. If you need a baby seat, ask for it in your request: each one is {{baby}} a day, capped at {{babyCap}}.

## Kilometres and fuel

If you are flying in for a week and driving across Ontario, check the kilometres included on the car's page. The daily allowance is added up over the rental, so a long first day is fine. Return the car with the fuel or charge it had at pickup, and fill up near the airport before the return rather than on the way out of the city.

## Other ways to start

If you would rather not drive at the airport at all, take the UP Express train to Union Station and have us meet you near the station, or have the car delivered to your hotel after you check in. Each of these is priced in your offer.

articles.title: Monthly vs weekly car rental in Toronto: which costs less

articles.description: How CarmaCars prices rentals of a week, a few weeks and a month, where the weekly and monthly caps apply, and how kilometres, deposits and renewals work.
articles.summary: A plain explanation of the weekly and monthly caps, and how to pick the length that costs least.
articles.body_md:
If you need a car for more than a few days, the length you book can change the price a lot. CarmaCars uses four rates for every car: a daily rate, a weekend day rate, a weekly rate and a monthly rate. This guide explains how they fit together, so you can choose the cheapest way to book.

## The four rates

Each car's page shows its rates:

- **Daily:** for days that start Monday to Thursday, and Sunday.
- **Weekend day:** for days that start on a Friday or a Saturday.
- **Weekly:** the price of a week.
- **Monthly:** the price of {{maxDays}} days, the longest single booking.

A rental day is 24 hours from your pickup time, and a part day counts as a day.

## The weekly cap

A short trip at the daily rate can cost more than a week. So we cap it: a trip of 1 to {{weekFromLess1}} days never costs more than the car's weekly rate. If you need a car for five days, check the weekly rate before you book. You may find the week costs the same, and you get the extra days for nothing.

## The monthly cap

The same rule applies above a week. A trip of {{weekFrom}} to {{maxDaysLess1}} days never costs more than the car's monthly rate. If you need a car for three weeks, the monthly rate may be the better deal, and you can keep the car for the full {{maxDays}} days.

Your offer shows exactly which rate applies to each day, so you always see the final number before you pay.

## Kilometres over a longer rental

Each car has a daily kilometre allowance. Over a rental, it is multiplied by the number of days you book and shared across the whole trip. On a monthly rental, that is a lot of driving: a long road trip in the first week is fine as long as the total stays within the allowance. Past it, extra kilometres are charged at the rate on the car's page, between {{overMin}} and {{overMax}} each depending on the car.

## Deposits on longer rentals

For rentals of {{holdDays}} days or less, the deposit is a hold on your card. For longer rentals it is charged and refunded after you return the car, within {{releaseDays}}. When you renew a monthly rental, the deposit carries over.

## Renewing a monthly rental

A single booking can run for up to {{maxDays}} days. If you need the car longer, tell us before the rental ends. We prepare a new agreement for the next period at the rate in force, you sign it online, and the next payment is taken. You keep the same car unless you ask to change.

## When weekly makes more sense

If you are not sure how long you need the car, book the shorter period and extend it. An extension is priced before you pay, and it must be paid before the current return time. For anything past about three weeks, compare the weekly and monthly totals in the offer: the cap does the work for you.

## Saving a little more

If your dates are fixed, choose the non-refundable option when you send your request. It takes {{nonRef}} off the rental charge, but it is not refunded if you cancel. And if you can collect the car from our location, you save the delivery fee.

faq.answer: {{maxDays}} days. You can renew with a new agreement before it ends.

faq.answer: No. Each car has a daily allowance, added up over the rental. Extra kilometres are charged at the car's rate.

faq.question: Does the deposit carry over when I renew?
faq.answer: Yes. It stays in place for the next period.

articles.title: Winter driving in Ontario in a rental car
articles.seo_title: Winter Driving in Ontario in a Rental Car
articles.description: How to drive a rental car safely through an Ontario winter: winter tires, clearing snow, trips north of Toronto, electric cars in the cold and more.
articles.summary: Practical advice for renting and driving in snow, ice and cold, from the people who hand the cars over.
articles.body_md:
An Ontario winter can turn a short drive into a slow one. Snow, ice and early darkness change how a car behaves and how long a trip takes. Most winter rentals go without a problem, and a little preparation makes the difference. This guide covers what we see most often at handovers.

## Winter tires

All-season tires lose grip as the temperature drops. Winter tires stay softer in the cold and grip much better on snow and ice. If you are driving outside the city, in the snow belts north of Toronto, or early in the morning on untreated roads, ask for winter tires in your request. The fee is {{winter}} a day, capped at {{winterCap}} for the rental.

## Before you set off

- Clear all the snow and ice from the windows, the mirrors, the lights and the roof. Snow sliding off the roof onto the windshield can blind you at the first stop.
- Check that the washer fluid works. Salt spray covers a windshield in minutes on the highway.
- Make sure there is a snow brush in the car. Ask at the handover if you do not see one.
- Turn on the headlights, not just the daytime running lights, so you are seen from behind.

## On the road

Leave much more space than usual between you and the car in front. Brake and turn gently, and slow down well before corners and ramps. Bridges and overpasses freeze before the road around them. If the car starts to slide, look and steer where you want to go, and do not stamp on the brakes.

Check road conditions before a longer trip. Ontario 511 shows closures and conditions on provincial highways. Snow squalls off the Great Lakes can bring sudden whiteouts, especially north of Barrie and along the 401 west of the city.

## Electric and hybrid cars in the cold

Cold weather shortens an electric car's range, sometimes by a lot. Plan longer winter trips with a charging stop, and keep some margin. Pre-heating the car while it is plugged in saves battery for the road. Return the car with the charge it had at pickup: recharging costs {{evPer}} for each 10% of battery, plus a {{fuelFee}} service fee. A hybrid is less affected by the cold and needs no charging.

## Choosing a car for winter

If your trip takes you out of the city, a car with all-wheel drive and a little more ground clearance copes better with unploughed side roads and cottage driveways. Each car's page lists its drive. All-wheel drive helps the car move off and stay straight, but it does not help it stop: winter tires matter more than the drive.

## Parking in a snowstorm

When the City of Toronto declares a major snowstorm, parking is banned on the streets marked as snow routes, and cars left there can be ticketed and towed. Check the signs where you park, and move the car if a storm is coming. Tickets and towing during a rental are the renter's, plus {{ticketFee}} for each ticket we process.

## If something goes wrong

Roadside assistance is included in every rental, around the clock. If the car breaks down or gets stuck, get to a safe place and call the number on your agreement. If there is a collision, make sure everyone is safe, call the police if anyone is hurt or the road is blocked, and tell us as soon as you can. Take photos of the scene and of the other car's plate.

## The car stays in Ontario

The car can go anywhere in Ontario. Driving into Quebec or the United States needs our written agreement first, so ask in your request if your plans include it.

articles.description: How a replacement rental works in Ontario when your car is in the shop after a claim, what your adjuster may approve, and how CarmaCars bills your insurer.
articles.summary: When your own car is off the road after a claim, your auto policy may pay for a rental. Here is how it usually works.
articles.body_md:
After a collision or a theft, the repair can take days or weeks. Your auto policy may pay for a replacement car in the meantime, and CarmaCars can bill your insurer directly for the part it approves. This guide explains how it usually works in Ontario and what to ask your adjuster. Your own policy and your adjuster have the final word on what is covered.

## Is a rental covered?

It depends on the claim and your policy:

- **If another driver was at fault**, your own insurer usually handles your claim for the damage to your car, and that can include a replacement car while it is repaired.
- **If you were at fault, or no other driver was involved**, a rental is usually covered only if your policy includes loss of use coverage, an optional endorsement many drivers add.

Ask your adjuster early: whether a rental is covered, for how many days, and up to what amount a day. Those three answers decide how much the insurer pays.

## What to send us

When you send your request, add in the notes:

- your insurance company and the claim number,
- your adjuster's name and how to reach them,
- the number of days approved and the daily amount, if you know them.

We confirm the car and the dates with you, contact the adjuster if needed, and send the invoice for the approved part to the insurer.

## What you still provide

A replacement rental is still a rental. You need an Ontario {{licence}} licence, a credit card in your name for the deposit, and your signature on the rental agreement. You also need coverage for damage to our car before pickup, one of the three options on our requirements page; your adjuster can tell you whether your own policy extends to the rental.

## What you may pay yourself

The insurer pays what it approves. You pay anything beyond that, for example:

- days after the approval ends, if the repair runs late and the approval is not extended,
- a car above the daily amount the insurer allows,
- fuel, tolls, tickets and other charges during the rental.

If the repair is taking longer, tell your adjuster and us before the approval ends. Extra days are yours to pay unless the insurer extends the approval.

## Choosing the car

Adjusters often approve a car of a size similar to yours, up to a daily amount. Tell us the amount, and we suggest cars within it. If you want a larger car, you can pay the difference yourself; the offer shows what the insurer pays and what you pay.

## Delivery to you or the body shop

We can deliver the car to your home, your work or the body shop, so you are not left without a car between drop-off and pickup. When your own car is ready, we collect ours from wherever suits you, or you bring it back to our location at no charge.

## Returning the car

Return the car with the fuel it had at pickup, and take your things out. We check it with you and photograph it, as at pickup. Charges that arrive later, such as tolls or parking tickets, are yours, not the insurer's, and are charged to the card on file with their administration fees.

faq.answer: Often, if another driver was at fault or your policy includes loss of use coverage. Your adjuster can confirm what you are covered for.

faq.answer: Yes, for the days and the daily amount your adjuster approves.

faq.question: Do I still need a credit card?
faq.answer: Yes, in your name, for the deposit and any charges the insurer does not cover.

faq.question: What if the repair takes longer than approved?
faq.answer: Ask your adjuster to extend the approval. Extra days are yours to pay unless it is extended.

articles.summary: Three of the most popular drives from Toronto, with what to check before you book the car.
articles.body_md:
A rental car is the easiest way to see more of Ontario than a train or a bus allows. Niagara Falls is an easy day trip, Ottawa is a long day or a relaxed weekend, and Montreal is a proper road trip. This guide covers the routes, the time on the road and the rental rules that matter for each.

## Niagara Falls

Niagara Falls is about 130 km from downtown Toronto. The usual route is the Gardiner Expressway west to the QEW, then the QEW around the end of Lake Ontario past Hamilton and St. Catharines. Without traffic it takes about an hour and a half; on a summer Friday or a holiday weekend it can take much longer, so leave early.

Parking near the falls is busy in summer. The wine region of Niagara-on-the-Lake is close by and makes a good stop on the way back.

The falls sit on the border with the United States. The car must not cross into the United States unless we have agreed in writing first.

## Ottawa

Ottawa is about 450 km from Toronto, most of it on the 401 east, then the 416 north from near Prescott. Plan on four and a half to five hours with a stop. The 401 between Toronto and Kingston is busy with trucks; Kingston and the Thousand Islands are good places to break the trip.

A return trip to Ottawa is about 900 km. Check the kilometres included on the car's page, multiply by the days you book, and make sure the total covers the drive.

## Montreal

Montreal is about 540 km from Toronto by the 401, which becomes Autoroute 20 at the Quebec border. It takes around five and a half to six hours with a stop. Montreal is in Quebec, so driving there needs our written agreement before the trip. Ask for it in your request and we confirm it in your offer.

Road signs in Quebec are in French. Turning right on a red light is not allowed on the island of Montreal.

## Kilometres

Each car includes a daily kilometre allowance, added up over the whole rental. A long drive on one day is fine as long as the total stays within the allowance. Past it, each kilometre costs between {{overMin}} and {{overMax}}, depending on the car. For a long trip, a car with a higher daily allowance, or an extra day on the booking, can cost less than the extra kilometres.

## Tolls and fuel

The QEW and the 401 are free. The 407 ETR is a toll road with no booths, and its tolls are billed to us and charged to you at cost plus {{tollFee}} for each notice. Switch on the avoid tolls setting in your map app if you would rather not use it.

Return the car with the fuel or charge it had at pickup. If it is lower, refuelling costs the pump price plus {{fuelPct}}, plus a {{fuelFee}} service fee, so a quick stop before the return usually saves money.

## Sharing the driving

On a long trip it helps to take turns. Add every driver to your request: each one meets the same rules, signs the agreement and adds {{addDrvPct}} of the daily rate for each day. Only drivers named on the agreement may drive.

faq.question: Can I drive a rental car from Toronto to Montreal?
faq.answer: Yes, with our written agreement before the trip, because the car normally stays in Ontario. Ask in your request.

faq.question: Can I take the rental car into the United States?
faq.answer: Only with our written agreement first.

faq.question: How far is Niagara Falls from Toronto?
faq.answer: About 130 km, or about an hour and a half without traffic.

faq.question: What happens if I go over the kilometres included?
faq.answer: Each extra kilometre is charged at the rate on the car's page, between {{overMin}} and {{overMax}}.

articles.brief: Road trips: Niagara Falls (about 130 km by the QEW, about 90 minutes), Ottawa (about 450 km by the 401 and the 416, 4.5 to 5 hours), Montreal (about 540 km by the 401 and A-20, 5.5 to 6 hours); leaving Ontario needs written agreement; kilometres, tolls, fuel, additional drivers.
